items.title: Workgraph draft storage identity is explicit
items.statement: The registry materializes a launch-critical redb family keyed by project, compile run, workgraph, and revision; it binds canonical MessagePack schema pm.storage_value.workgraph_draft.v1 version 1.0.0 to owner PNC-013.

items.title: Workgraph draft producer and consumers are named
items.statement: PlanCompile graph draft stage produces the value; WorkNodeRequest derivation, graph integrity validation, and Goal Runtime certification consume it.

items.title: Workgraph top-level envelope is closed and required
items.statement: The value is a closed object whose required envelope covers identity, graph payload, scheduling, integrity, authority, evidence, validation, timestamp, and redaction; supersedes_revision alone is optional and nullable with a minimum of one when present.

items.title: Replay is inspection-only until PNC-019
items.statement: Replay restores revisions only for inspection and validation, and activation remains blocked until PNC-019.

evidence.exact_quote: "replay_behavior": "Replay restores graph draft revisions for inspection and validation only; activation stays blocked until PNC-019.",

items.title: Workgraph revision migration and evidence retention are explicit
items.statement: Shape changes require a family-version increment and continued reachability of prior revisions; any revision referenced by compile, request, or Goal evidence is retained.

evidence.exact_quote:
"migration": "Any value-shape change increments workgraph_draft family version and preserves prior revision reachability.",
      "retention_compaction": "Retain every revision referenced by PlanCompileRun, WorkNodeRequest, or Goal receipt evidence.",

items.title: Workgraph secret boundary and non-executable status are explicit
items.statement: Graph values contain references and readiness metadata rather than raw provider output or local secret-bearing content, and the stored draft is explicitly not an executable WorkGraph.

evidence.exact_quote:
"redaction_no_secret_rule": "Graph nodes carry refs and readiness metadata, not raw provider output or local secret-bearing file content.",
      "legacy_canonical_crosswalk_status": "Canonical draft graph storage row; not a materialized executable WorkGraph.",

items.title: Workgraph node and edge records have no contract
items.statement: Nodes and dependency edges are arrays of unconstrained objects. The registry does not define node identity, dependency endpoints, per-node readiness, duplicate handling, or reference integrity, even though those values feed graph validation and request derivation.
items.impact: Independent builders can encode mutually incompatible graphs that all satisfy this schema, preventing deterministic validation and derivation.
items.builder_discretion: Object members, identity keys, endpoint representation, uniqueness, and referential-integrity rules are all left to implementation.

items.title: Workgraph policy, integrity, authority, and validation states are opaque
items.statement: Scheduler policy, graph integrity, authority, and validation state are required but unconstrained objects. No state vocabulary, transition guards, decision authority, integrity algorithm, or failure/recovery behavior is encoded.
items.impact: Activation gating, authorization, scheduling, and validation cannot be implemented or certified consistently from this registry.
items.builder_discretion: Builders choose every property and semantic rule for four launch-critical objects.

items.title: WorkNodeRequest storage identity and ownership are explicit
items.statement: The registry materializes a launch-critical redb request family keyed by project, workgraph, and request, encoded as canonical MessagePack schema pm.storage_value.worknode_request.v1 version 1.0.0 and owned by PNC-014.

items.title: WorkNodeRequest producer and consumers are named

items.title: Request collections permit empty and blank semantic inputs
items.statement: Lineage refs, implementation surfaces, read/write candidates, acceptance criteria, validators, dependencies, and capability requirements are arrays of unconstrained strings with no minimum cardinality, nonblank-string constraint, uniqueness, or reference format.
items.impact: A structurally valid launch-critical request can carry no lineage, no acceptance criteria, no validators, or blank/duplicate references and still reach intake consumers.
items.builder_discretion: Builders decide which collections may be empty, how references are formatted, and whether duplicates or blank values are rejected.

items.title: Routing, testing, ordering, authority, and cancellation contracts are opaque
items.statement: The request requires test_binding, model_routing, ordering_metadata, authority, and cancellation_policy but defines each only as an unconstrained object. No routing eligibility, test oracle binding, precedence, authorization, cancellation state, acknowledgment, or recovery semantics are specified.
items.impact: Executor intake and certification cannot reach deterministic, interoperable decisions for required request policies.
items.builder_discretion: Every property and semantic rule of five required policy objects is left to each implementation.

items.title: Idempotency key has syntax but no behavior
items.statement: idempotency_key is only a nonempty string. Its uniqueness scope, derivation, collision handling, duplicate-request response, expiry, and interaction with revision or replay are undefined.
items.impact: Retries and replay can create divergent or duplicate intake effects across implementations.
items.builder_discretion: The deduplication domain and all duplicate/collision behavior are implementation-defined.

items.title: GUI and frontend flags have no truth rule
items.statement: gui_related and frontend_related are required booleans, but the source supplies no classification criteria, derivation authority, consistency invariant, or downstream behavior for their four combinations.
items.impact: The same request may be routed, validated, or presented differently depending on a builder's interpretation of the flags.
items.builder_discretion: Classification and conflict resolution are entirely implementation-defined.

items.title: Blocked and denied request states lack a state model
items.statement: Replay refers to pending requests, retention refers to denied requests and rejection receipts, and blocked_reason_refs is optional, yet the value has no request-status field or rules connecting these concepts to state transitions, reason requirements, retryability, or recovery.
items.impact: Consumers cannot determine a request's authoritative state or reproduce denial, blocking, retry, and recovery transitions.
items.builder_discretion: State vocabulary, transition guards, reason cardinality, and receipt linkage are not fixed.

items.title: Acceptance and validation oracles are not executable contracts
items.statement: Acceptance criteria and validator candidates are free-form strings, test_binding is opaque, and workgraph validation_state is opaque. The registry provides structural validation but no pass/fail oracle, validator identity/version binding, result format, or evidence requirement.
items.impact: Implementation-readiness and Goal Runtime certification cannot be reproduced from the values alone.
items.builder_discretion: Validator selection, execution, expected result, and evidence sufficiency are left open.

items.title: No scale or performance bounds constrain launch-critical values
items.statement: Graph and request collections have no maxItems, byte-size, depth, fan-out, string-length, or processing-time bounds; unconstrained nested objects compound this absence.
items.impact: Storage, canonical encoding, validation, replay, and intake costs are unbounded by the contract.
items.builder_discretion: Each implementation chooses admission limits and overload behavior.

items.title: Migration rules do not define compatibility execution
items.statement: Both families require version changes, and workgraph drafts preserve prior revision reachability, but the source does not define reader compatibility, migration ordering, atomicity, rollback, failure receipts, or how old and new versions coexist.
items.impact: Version transitions can produce inconsistent reads or intake behavior despite satisfying the stated version-increment rules.
items.builder_discretion: Compatibility windows, conversion procedures, failure recovery, and rollback are unspecified.

items.title: Retention statements omit compaction and deletion oracles
items.statement: The registry states what referenced evidence must be retained, but not how preservation is proven, when unreferenced data may be compacted, how reachability is computed, or what happens on partial compaction failure.
items.impact: Operators cannot implement deterministic safe compaction or certify that deletion preserves required evidence.
items.builder_discretion: Reachability scans, grace periods, tombstones, deletion receipts, and recovery behavior are open.

items.title: Cross-family propagation and atomicity are unspecified
items.statement: The workgraph family is consumed to derive requests and both values are tied into validation/certification, but the source gives no atomic commit boundary, revision pinning rule, stale-input response, causal link, or retry/compensation protocol across the producer-consumer chain.
items.impact: Request derivation and certification may observe different graph revisions or duplicate/lose effects during retries and failures.
items.builder_discretion: Builders choose transaction boundaries, consistency model, staleness policy, and compensating behavior.

dimension_assessments.summary: Replay and non-executable boundaries are explicit, but idempotency, cancellation, blocked/denied handling, and cross-family behavior remain undefined.
The two families support draft graph storage and intake request storage, but their core graph and policy capabilities are opaque.
Top-level inputs are named, but collection cardinality, reference format, nested graph shape, and policy outputs are not constrained.
Closed top-level envelopes and version identities exist, while launch-critical nested schemas and semantic invariants are missing.
PNC-019 blocking is explicit, but graph validation and request pending/blocked/denied/cancelled state machines are not.
Owner documents are named, but required authority objects have no principal, scope, decision, precedence, or verification schema.
PNC-013 owns workgraph_draft and PNC-014 owns worknode_request; producers are also explicit.
Both families enumerate their immediate validation, derivation, intake, readiness, and certification consumers.
Required GUI/frontend booleans exist without classification or downstream truth semantics.
Replay and rejection-receipt retention are mentioned, but failure states, retryability, cancellation recovery, migration rollback, and compaction recovery are unspecified.
Both families exclude raw provider/local secret material and restrict redaction_profile to two enumerated values.
Producer-consumer chains are named, but no atomicity, revision pinning, staleness, retry, or compensation protocol connects them.
Retention intent exists without compaction/deletion oracles, and migration lacks operational sequencing and rollback.
No size, cardinality, fan-out, depth, latency, or overload constraints bound either launch-critical value.
Version increments and prior reachability are required, but read compatibility, coexistence, conversion, rollback, and failure handling are absent.
Structural schema checks are present, but semantic integrity, acceptance, validation, certification, and evidence oracles are not executable contracts.
Consequential discretion remains over graph structure, required policies, idempotency, state models, GUI classification, bounds, propagation, migration, and compaction.
Opaque objects and unbound lifecycle terms leave multiple incompatible but schema-valid interpretations of the stored values.
